candidates.name: Ashley Hinson
candidates.background: U.S. Representative since 2021 (IA-01, then IA-02 after redistricting); former TV news anchor. Won the June 2026 Republican primary for the open seat.

immigration.label: Voted for H.R. 2 (Secure the Border Act); backs increased border funding (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Supports making the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Backs renewables/biofuels without 'unfair taxes' or regulation; voted for the Lower Energy Costs Act; opposes the Green New Deal (Ballotpedia)

cost.label: 'Make life more affordable by cutting wasteful spending, lowering inflation, and creating an economy where small businesses can grow' (campaign issues)

housing.label: Tax-free first-time homebuyer savings and 'ensuring large institutional investors cannot buy up single-family homes in Iowa neighborhoods' (campaign issues)

education.label: 'Protect parents' rights by giving families a stronger voice in their children's education'; more school transparency (campaign issues)

safety.label: 'Combat fentanyl and violent crime by cracking down on traffickers, strengthening partnerships with law enforcement' (campaign issues)

repro.label: Voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, H.R. 26, passed 220-210 (House roll call 29, 2023)

democracy.label: Voted for the SAVE Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, passed 220-208 (House roll call 102, 2025)

candidates.name: Mariannette Miller-Meeks
candidates.background: Mariannette Miller-Meeks is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Iowa's 1st District, an ophthalmologist and 24-year U.S. Army veteran who also served as director of the Iowa Department of Public Health and as a state senator. In Congress since 2021 (2nd District 2021-2023, 1st District since 2023), she won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary with 71.6% over David Pautsch with President Trump's endorsement.

sources.label: Iowa Starting Line: abortion position analysis

priorities: Energy independence through all domestic sources

cost.label: Championed the 'Working Families Tax Cuts,' called 'the largest tax relief for working and middle-class Americans in U.S. history,' plus deregulation to cut costs (House office issues page)

health.label: Prices on the Wall Act requires providers to post prices; PBM reform via the DRUG Act (House office issues page)

housing.label: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which she championed, 'cuts red tape, builds more homes, lowers costs' via fewer regulatory barriers (House office press release)

immigration.label: Voted yes on S.5 Laken Riley Act mandating DHS detention of aliens charged with theft, passed 264-134 (House roll call 23, Jan 22, 2025)

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R.1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act extending the 2017 tax cuts, passed 218-214 (House roll call 190, Jul 3, 2025)

climate.label: 'American energy should remain in American hands': led effort to protect fracking, voted to expand LNG exports, opposed the EV mandate (House office energy page)

education.label: Cosponsored the Educational Choice for Children Act, '$10 billion in annual tax credits to incentivize education choice for K-12 students' (House office education page)

safety.label: Touted the One Big Beautiful Bill's law-enforcement provisions at a campaign event: 'No tax on overtime is a raise for every police officer,' plus $750M for law enforcement training (WBBJ campaign coverage)

repro.label: Supports a national 15-week abortion ban, praised Iowa's near-total ban, and cosponsored the no-exceptions Life at Conception Act in 2021 (Iowa Starting Line)

democracy.label: Voted yes on H.R.22 SAVE Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, passed 220-208 (House roll call 102, Apr 10, 2025)

candidates.name: Christina Bohannan
candidates.background: Christina Bohannan is a University of Iowa law professor and former Iowa House member who worked as an environmental engineer before her legal career. She lost this seat to Miller-Meeks by roughly 800 votes in 2024 and won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 81.5% over Travis Terrell for the rematch.

cost.label: 'Iowans are struggling to make ends meet': plans to end tariffs and 'crack down on price gouging' (campaign priorities page)

health.label: Supports letting Iowans buy into Medicare at any age while keeping private insurance options and capping insulin at $35/month; opposes single-payer (campaign priorities page)

housing.label: Plans to prohibit hedge funds and private investors from 'purchasing family homes and artificially raising rents' while building and rehabilitating more housing (campaign priorities page)

taxes.label: Calls tariffs 'one of the biggest tax increases in American history,' opposes 'billionaire tax giveaways,' and backs closing corporate loopholes (campaign priorities page)

climate.label: Backs clean-energy expansion and water-quality investment for farmers hit by 'heat, drought, and extreme weather' (campaign priorities page)

education.label: 'Make Iowa number one in public education again' through reinvestment, opposing voucher programs that 'drain resources' (campaign priorities page)

repro.label: 'I will fight every day to put Roe v. Wade back into federal law' against Iowa's six-week ban (campaign priorities page)

democracy.label: Backs 'the Let America Vote Act to allow the 33% of Iowans who are independents to participate in primaries' (campaign priorities page)

candidates.name: Zach Nunn
candidates.background: Zach Nunn is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Iowa's 3rd District, a U.S. Air Force veteran and former cybersecurity official who served on the White House National Security Council and in the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. A former state legislator, he has held the seat since 2023 after winning races decided by fewer than four points.

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R.1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act extending the 2017 tax cuts, passed 218-214 (House roll call 190, Jul 3, 2025)

democracy.label: Voted yes on H.R.22 SAVE Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, passed 220-208 (House roll call 102, Apr 10, 2025)
